newsitem.title: KENYA: Illegal imports seen undermining Kenya sugar.
newsitem.headline: Illegal imports seen undermining Kenya sugar.

text.p: Corruption at ports and poor policing helped illegal sugar imports into Kenya, avoiding taxes imposed to protect domestic producers, Agriculture Minister Simeon Nyachae said on Tuesday.
"Corrupt elements are getting sugar in, business thugs are undermining the domestic industry," he told a news conference.
Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) officials say thousands of tonnes of sugar have been offloaded onto the Kenyan market this year after first registering at ports as being in transit.
On Monday, KRA officials seized more than 25,000 tonnes of sugar in Mombasa.
"The sugar was supposed to be on transit. We are seeking verification," said the Mombasa-based Ali Hafidh, Assistant Commissioner of Customs and Excise, southern region.

Last week, KRA officers impounded 7,400 tonnes of sugar they said was also meant to be in transit. They said they were monitoring sugar movement at the port because of rising incidents of transit sugar being diverted to domestic use.
In the past month, some 60,000 tonnes of sugar have been offloaded at Mombasa for the Kenyan market, despite heavy taxes.
Neither the Kenya Ports Authority nor the Kenya Revenue Authority had the total of sugar imports so far this year.
But an official at the Mumias Sugar Company, Kenya's chief miller, said they were unable to sell 20,000 tonnes of sugar they imported in June because the domestic market was flooded.
Mumias had imported the sugar in anticipation of domestic shortages after it closed the mill for repairs in May-June.
The Kenya Sugar Authority has posted production at 384,171 tonnes in 1995 from 303,292 tonnes in 1994 and sees a jump to 420,000 tonnes in 1996 on better weather and management.
Nyachae said cane production had risen to 4.394 million tonnes in 1995 from 3.081 million in 1995 and 3.839 million in 1994. He gave no forecast for 1996.
The Sugar Authority says domestic demand had risen to 560,000 tonnes this year from 348,678 tonnes in 1984.
